bigSave: The hedge paid out. Somewhere, a sceptical CFO quietly deletes an angry email.
Hedged before the storm. Treasury is briefly the most popular department in the building.
Your forwards earned their keep. Expect zero thanks and one extra audit question.
The market swung. Your hedges swung back. Nobody outside treasury will ever know.
Saved by the hedge. That's the slide for next year's conference panel.
A textbook save. Someone will put it in a textbook and misspell your name.
Protected. The kind of quarter that makes 'boring' sound like a compliment.
Hedge accounting just became a pleasure. Remember this feeling. It's rare.
bigMiss: The market went your way. You politely hedged it away.
Unhedged would have won. Hindsight is 20/20 and it's sitting on the board.
You bought an umbrella. It was sunny. The board would like a word about umbrellas.
Opportunity cost: never on an invoice, always in the board pack.
The hedge did its job. Unfortunately, this quarter its job was to cost money.
Somewhere a speculator is buying a boat with the move you hedged away.
Insurance this quarter, and the house didn't burn down. Annoying, isn't it?
overHedged: You hedged more than you sold. That's not a hedge, it's a hobby.
Forecast optimism meets reality. The extra forwards are now a position. Congratulations.
Over-hedged. The excess is speculation, and the auditors have a word for it.
Sales came in light; the hedges didn't. 'Forecast' and 'wish' are different words.
You hedged 100% of a forecast that turned out to be fan fiction.
The business sold less than it promised. Shocking. Nobody has ever seen that before.
Hedged above actuals. The board calls that a bet with extra paperwork.
nearBankrupt: Below the red line. Your relationship manager has stopped returning calls.
Liquidity: low. Like your phone battery at 3% during the closing keynote.
The red line is behind you. The overdraft is in front of you. Choose wisely.
Below the red line. The credit insurers have started using the word 'concerned'.
Cash is so tight the office plants are on a watering rota.
The lenders are reading the covenants aloud. Slowly. With emphasis.
Treasury now forecasts cash by the hour. Daily was for the good times.
calm: A quiet quarter. The most underrated outcome in treasury.
Nothing dramatic happened. Frame it. It won't last.
Markets moved, you didn't panic. Quietly excellent. Nobody will mention it.
Calm, like the coffee queue five minutes before the keynote ends.
Steady. The board barely looked up from their phones. That's a win.
Volatility took the quarter off. Probably stuck in the lanyard queue.
Uneventful. In treasury, that's the highest form of praise.
Nothing to see here. Exactly how a treasurer likes it.
boom: The market moved your way. Act like you planned it. Everyone else does.
A tailwind quarter. Accept the compliments. Deflect the questions.
A big favourable move. The CEO will call it 'strategy' on the earnings call.
Windfall! Sales will claim it by Friday. Procurement by Thursday.
Lovely move. Enjoy it before someone asks you to forecast the next one.
Lucky market, happy board. Don't tell them those two things are related.
Boom. The board is so pleased they almost read the treasury report.

moodUp: Good. Our competitors would kill for that quarter. Let them.
That's the treasurer I hired. Don't make me regret saying it out loud.
Finally, numbers I can wave at the analysts. Keep them coming.
Decent. Now do it again, faster, and with fewer meetings.
I'll be taking credit for this at the AGM. You understand.
Acceptable. I'm upgrading you from 'concern' to 'watch list'.
moodDown: That's not a quarter. That's an apology with a spreadsheet attached.
Our competitors are laughing. I can hear them from the exhibition hall.
I didn't fly in for this. Well, I flew in for the golf. But still.
Explain it to me slowly. Then explain it faster, so I can leave.
If this is a strategy, it's hiding very well.
Do better. I don't care how. That's literally your job.
redZone: We're below the red line. I want cash, a plan, and nobody hearing about it.
The bank phoned ME. Do you know how rarely that's good news?
Red line breached. I'm cancelling the Christmas party. And possibly Christmas.
Cash this low makes me nervous. I don't do nervous. I do shouting.
Fix the cash, or I fix the org chart.
The red line exists for a reason. Get back above it. Today.
luckyBreach: Great result. Never do that again. Or do it again, but tell me first.
Superb numbers, shocking method. I'm proud and furious. Pick one.
You broke the mandate and made money. I'll applaud quietly. Then I'll shout.
Brilliant outcome. Terrible precedent. The minutes record both, in capitals.
I love the profit. I hate the route. Keep one of those.
It worked, you cowboy. Next time, work inside the lines. Well done though.
breachLoss: Outside the mandate AND losing money? HR is booking a meeting room. A small one.
You gambled with my company and lost. Put your lanyard on the table.
Off-policy losses. The board isn't angry. The board is drafting.
You ignored the policy and torched our cash. HR says 'process'. I say 'out'.
I asked HR how fast we can do this. They said 'faster than your hedges paid out'.
Speculating with company money and losing it? That's a career, ending.
The policy exists so this never happens. It happened. Check your access card works.
inPolicyBad: We agreed the policy. I still hate it. Quarter's noted. Move on.
Bad quarter, but we stayed in the lines. I'll shout at the market instead.
The policy did its job. My blood pressure did not.
Painful. But nobody can say you broke the rules. Annoying, that.
I'm irritated, not furious. The policy gets the credit. You get the blame.
Rough. The hedge did what we signed up for. I just wanted a better quarter.
Within policy, so I can't even shout at you. I'm shouting at the market.
noPolicyHedgeLoss: The hedge LOST money? Who approved this? Oh. You did.
We hedged and we lost. Why did we pay for protection that costs money?
A loss on the hedge! Unwind it. Unwind all of it. Immediately.
I don't care what it protected. The hedge line is red. Fix the line.
Explain this hedge loss. Slowly. Without the word 'offset'.
Hedging is meant to make money. This one didn't. I'm writing that down.
The business is fine, you say? Then why is this one number red?
noPolicyHedgeWin: The hedge made money. So... we should hedge everything? Is that how it works?
A hedge gain. Good. Do that again. Every quarter. Nothing else.
We won on the hedge! Why did you wait so long? I'm joking. Mostly.
Fine, it paid off. I still don't understand why. Don't explain it.
Hedge profit. I'm told that's a coincidence. I'm calling it skill.
The hedge went up. I'd like it to go up more, please.
Well, that's a number I can show the analysts. Whatever it is.
noPolicyNudge: We have no hedging policy. Draw one up, and make it quick.
Every quarter we argue about hedges. A policy would end that. Propose one.
Bring me a hedging policy. One page. Big font. Pictures welcome.
No policy means I judge each hedge alone. You won't enjoy it. Propose one.
Write a hedging policy and I'll sign it. Probably. Maybe without reading.
Right now we're winging it. Propose a policy before I start winging you.
policyAdopted: Policy adopted from next quarter. I'd like it noted that this was my idea.
Approved. A proper policy at last. I knew we were an organised company.
Policy accepted. Now we have rules, and I get to enforce them.
Done. From next quarter we're a grown-up board. Don't let it show.
Adopted unanimously, because I was the only one who read it.
A policy! The analysts will love this. I'll tell them I wrote it.

moodUp: The figures reconcile. I've checked twice. Well done.
Within limits and profitable. I may permit myself a second biscuit.
A clean quarter. The auditors will be almost disappointed.
Variance within tolerance. My favourite four words.
I've minuted this as 'satisfactory'. Please don't let it go to your head.
Disciplined and documented. Exactly as the policy intended.
moodDown: I'd like a root-cause analysis. And then an analysis of the analysis.
This variance will need a footnote. Possibly a chapter.
I flagged this risk two quarters ago. Page 14 of the minutes.
The risk committee will want a word. Several words. Mostly 'why'.
I don't enjoy surprises. This one was expensive and unscheduled.
We'll need a lessons-learned session. I've booked three.
redZone: Cash is below the red line. I've already drafted the covenant waiver request.
Our liquidity headroom is now a rounding error. This is not a drill.
Below the red line. Cash forecasting moves to daily. Then hourly.
The bank has asked for management accounts early. That's never good.
We're under the red line. I'd like a 13-week cash flow forecast by tonight.
Red line breached. I haven't slept, and I've made a spreadsheet about it.
luckyBreach: A fine result, and a clear breach. I commend the one and minute the other.
Welcome profit, unwelcome process. Praise and a reprimand, in the same memo.
Good outcome. Poor controls. I'll thank you and write you up in one email.
Commendable return. Unacceptable authority. I shall send two letters.
The result pleases me. The method disturbs me. The audit committee agrees with both.
Well done on the gain. Do not do it again. I have underlined 'not'.
breachLoss: A breach AND a loss. I've informed the audit committee and, frankly, HR.
Outside approved limits, with losses. I am recommending your dismissal.
I've documented this breach in full. HR has asked for a copy. So has legal.
Unauthorised positions, realised losses. Your trading limits are suspended.
This is exactly what the policy forbids. Please clear your desk by Monday.
Off-mandate losses. The committee will vote on replacing you. Unanimously, I expect.
inPolicyBad: A loss, but within the approved bands. The policy has worked as designed.
Disappointing, yet compliant. I'll minute it as 'unfortunate, not improper'.
We agreed the policy. I still hate it. But the process held.
The variance is regrettable. The control environment is intact. Slightly consoled.
Within policy, so no breach is recorded. The loss is recorded with sighing.
I'd have preferred a profit. I'd have preferred a better market too.
Adverse outcome, correct process. A lessons-learned session, but a short one.
noPolicyHedgeLoss: A hedge loss with no policy to explain it? This will need a formal inquiry.
The hedge lost money. Under what authority was it placed? Please cite the page.
I see a realised loss on a hedge. The exposure is irrelevant. The loss is red.
A loss on the hedging line. I'm opening an incident. And a second one.
Hedge P&L is negative. We have no policy to blame, so I'm blaming you.
Who approved a transaction that loses money by design? Oh, it's by design?
Without a policy, every hedge loss is a finding. This is finding number one.
noPolicyHedgeWin: The hedge gained. In the absence of a policy, I don't know how to feel.
A hedge profit. I've no framework to assess it. I'm uneasy. Pleasantly.
Positive hedge P&L. Please don't mention this until we have a policy.
A gain, without a policy. I don't enjoy unsupervised good news.
The hedge made money, apparently. I'll add 'understand why' to the agenda.
Hedge gains are welcome. Unexplained hedge gains go on the risk register.
noPolicyNudge: We have no hedging policy. This is an audit finding waiting to be written.
I recommend the CFO tables a hedging policy at the next meeting. Soon.
Without a policy, nothing you do can be called compliant. Propose one.
A hedging policy is overdue. I've left a draft template on your desk. Blank.
I'm unable to approve hedges against no policy. Please propose a policy.
The committee will consider any policy you propose. We have no other agenda.
policyAdopted: Policy adopted from next quarter. I have already filed it. Twice.
Approved and minuted. We now have a framework. I feel eight years younger.
The policy is adopted. I've scheduled its first review. For next week.
At last, a document. I shall read it, annotate it and laminate it.
Policy ratified. The auditors will send flowers. Possibly a questionnaire too.
Adopted. From next quarter, we may call things 'compliant' again.

moodUp: Good quarter. Can I have my capex request back out of the bin?
Stable costs! The factory floor might actually believe a forecast.
Nice. Procurement can stop hiding from the suppliers.
Predictable cash. I can plan production without crossing my fingers.
Good. The warehouse lights stay on another quarter.
Helpful. Suppliers love us when we pay on time.
moodDown: That loss just ate my maintenance budget. Again.
Every pound lost here is a pound I can't spend on spare parts.
Suppliers will hear about this. They always do. Then prices go up.
I don't understand derivatives, but I understand 'less money'.
My team's been asking for new kit. I'll tell them 'next year'. Again.
That makes Monday's supplier negotiation a lot harder.
redZone: Cash under the red line? I've got payroll on Friday.
Suppliers want paying up front now. Thanks for that.
We're so short on cash I'm rationing pallets. Actual pallets.
Below the red line. I've delayed a machine repair. It's making noises.
The bank's nervous, the suppliers are nervous, and now I'm nervous.
Low cash means the factory runs on hope. Hope is not a raw material.
luckyBreach: Great result. The CFO's eye is twitching. Please don't repeat it.
Good money, wrong route. The floor cheers, the rulebook weeps.
Nice gain, and I'm pleased. But we don't skip the checklist. Not even then.
You got the result, and a verbal warning. I'd take both, honestly.
It paid off, which I like. It was off-policy, which I don't. Thanks, and don't.
Cheers for the cash. Now put the rules back where you found them.
breachLoss: You broke the rules and lost my payroll money. HR wants a chat. Today.
Off-policy and in the red. On the floor, that's how you lose your pass.
That loss cancelled my new machine. HR has asked me about your 'judgement'.
No checklist, no policy, no money. I've asked HR what happens next.
Rule-breaking that costs money? Where I work, that's a final written warning.
You gambled the supplier payments and lost. Security has asked for your lanyard.
inPolicyBad: Bad quarter, but we followed the policy. I'll live. The kit won't.
We agreed the policy. I still hate it. At least nobody broke anything.
Money's tight, but the hedge did what it said. I can budget around that.
A loss inside the rules. I can explain that to the floor. Just about.
Stung, not shocked. The policy held. Maintenance gets cut by half instead of all.
Not great. But no surprises, and surprises are what scare me.
Policy worked, market didn't. I'll tell the team it's weather.
noPolicyHedgeLoss: The hedge LOST money? Who approved this? That was my spare-parts budget.
We paid for protection and it cost us? I'm not saying fire someone, but.
A hedge loss. I thought hedges were like insurance. Insurance doesn't lose.
The hedge is down. The fuel bill is steady. Why are we upset? Because red.
Hedge lost money. Cancel it. Cancel them all. I'm busy.
I don't care what it protected. That number is a machine I can't buy.
So we spent money to avoid spending money? And it cost money? Unwind it.
noPolicyHedgeWin: The hedge made money? Where was that when I needed a new forklift?
A hedge gain. Excellent. Can we hedge the canteen next?
We made money on a hedge. I'm told this is not what hedges are for. Fine.
The hedge paid. My team wants to know if we can do that every week.
A gain! I'll spend it before anybody explains it away.
Hedge profit. Nobody tell Procurement. They'll want a cut.
noPolicyNudge: We've got no hedging policy. Propose one so I can stop guessing.
Without a policy, I never know what's allowed. Write one. Short, please.
A hedging policy would save me ten meetings a quarter. Please propose one.
Every shop floor has rules. Treasury should too. Propose a policy.
No policy, no plan. Table a policy and I'll stop asking awkward questions.
Give us a hedging policy. Even a rough one. I'll laminate it myself.
policyAdopted: Policy adopted from next quarter. Finally, a rulebook I can pin on the wall.
Approved. Now everyone knows what the line is. Even me.
Done. We have a policy. I'll tell the floor. They won't care. I do.
Adopted. It's like a safety sign, but for money.
A policy! I can plan production around that. Or at least plan a tea break.
Policy in place from next quarter. I feel safer already. Slightly.

jameson: THIS KEYNOTE IS 40 MINUTES OVER! GET ME THE HEDGE NUMBERS! AND A SANDWICH!
I DON'T WANT A LANYARD! I WANT RESULTS!
HEDGE IT! UNHEDGE IT! I DON'T CARE! JUST GET ME A HEADLINE!
COFFEE! NUMBERS! IN THAT ORDER! MOVE!
Networking? I don't network. I SHOUT. There's a difference!
musk: What if the hedge book was a rocket? Just thinking out loud.
I've renamed the treasury department 'T'. New logo tonight.
Forwards are legacy tech. We're hedging with memes now.
I polled my followers. 60% voted to unhedge everything. Democracy.
Skipped the keynote. Gave my own in the coffee queue. Standing room only.
oleary: Free conference coffee? I've taken forty. Someone bring the van round.
Options? You want to PAY for a maybe? Absolutely not.
From next quarter the board pays to sit in the boardroom chairs. Fair's fair.
The lanyard was free. That's the only reason I'm wearing it.
Hedging's like legroom. Lovely to have. Now, who's paying for it?
dimon: Fortress balance sheet. That's the whole strategy. Write it down.
A good outcome isn't a good decision. Ask me how I know.
Show me the real risk report. Not the conference-stand version.
I've seen every crisis since '87. Your hedge ratio worries me more.
buffett: Price is what you pay for a hedge. Value is sleeping at night.
When the tide goes out, you find out who forgot to hedge.
I'd rather be approximately hedged than precisely wrong.
Our favourite holding period is forever. Our favourite keynote is short.
jobs: One more thing. Your hedge book has too many buttons.
Simplicity. One exposure, one hedge, one beautiful slide.
I wouldn't let my kids use this hedge book. That's a compliment. Mostly.
Design is how it works. Your hedges work. They just look terrible.
dorsey: I meditated through the market crash. The crash did not notice.
Day four of my fast, I understood basis risk. Day five, I forgot it.
Ice bath at 5am, board meeting at 9. Both equally cold.
Let's move the reserves into Bitcoin. I moved mine. I am very calm about it.
ackman: A brief comment. Page one of forty-seven.
I've posted my hedging thesis online. It's a thread. It's 112 posts long.
I'll keep it short. Slide one of my second deck.
High conviction: we're mispriced. Low conviction: we'll finish on time.

gameOverTitles.title: Unpaid Intern
gameOverTitles.line: You've earned a lanyard and supervised access to the stationery cupboard.

gameOverTitles.title: Spreadsheet Wrangler
gameOverTitles.line: VLOOKUP whisperer. The board knows your name. Roughly.

gameOverTitles.title: Treasury Analyst
gameOverTitles.line: Promising. You've been trusted with the coffee order and a hedge ratio.

gameOverTitles.title: Assistant Treasurer
gameOverTitles.line: Solid work. You now get invited to meetings you can't leave.

gameOverTitles.title: Group Treasurer
gameOverTitles.line: Respectable. The banks send you Christmas cards and conference invites.

gameOverTitles.title: Head of Treasury
gameOverTitles.line: The board trusts you. The auditors tolerate you. That's the dream.

gameOverTitles.title: Chief Financial Officer
gameOverTitles.line: Corner office, panel slot, 4,000 unread emails. You've made it.

gameOverTitles.title: Treasury Legend
gameOverTitles.line: Keynote material. You'll overrun by forty minutes and nobody will mind.

gameOverTitles.title: Master of the Hedge
gameOverTitles.line: Flawless. Bankers whisper your name in the coffee queue.

bankrupt: Out of cash. The CFO has been replaced, mostly by an administrator.
The bank has called. Nobody answered, because you were already in the lift.
Cash: zero. The CFO has been replaced. The replacement is a spreadsheet.
The bank has called the loans. Your lanyard still works until 5pm.
Insolvent. The banks stopped returning calls and started sending lawyers.
Bust. The CFO has been replaced, and the administrators brought their own biscuits.
Out of cash, out of time. The bank has called, and so has your replacement.
fired: The board has lost confidence in your results. Security will walk you out.
Overall results fell short, and one bet cost us dearly. The board is 'moving on'.
You're fired. The numbers didn't add up, and neither did your explanations.
The board's confidence has collapsed. So has your access card.
One catastrophic off-policy bet. The board is going in a different direction. Away.
The results speak for themselves. Unfortunately they speak to HR.
Your LinkedIn now says 'exploring new opportunities'. The board made sure of it.

band: Our policy is to hedge {band} of exposure. Stay inside it. Please.
The board expects {band} of exposures to be hedged. We have a spreadsheet.
Policy: hedge {band}. Below it you're reckless. Above it you're showing off.
Welcome. Hedge {band} of your exposure and we'll get on famously.
noHedge: Our policy is not to hedge. We believe in 'markets'. Mostly the lucky ones.
The board does not hedge. Hedging is for people who plan to lose.
Policy: no hedging. Any hedge you place had better be a very good story.
We don't hedge here. We hope, and we put it in the annual report.
none: We have no hedging policy. We judge every hedge on its own P&L. Good luck.
No policy, no bands, no mercy. Each hedge stands or falls on its own profit.
The board has no view on hedging, only on hedge profits. Propose a policy.
There's no policy. We just look at the hedge line and react. Strongly.
